meta.title: Netcap distributed capture: decode at the sensor, collect centrally

cards.title: Decode once, close to the traffic
items: net agent uses the capture collector with channel writers, then batches its serialized audit records (cmd/agent/main.go:121-184,215-224).

The diagram shows one sensor path; multiple separately enrolled sensors use the same server. The collector assigns output identity from its allowlist, not from the agent's chosen name (identity.go:297-309).
Extracted content, logs and enabled behavioral state can still remain on the sensor (docs/distributed-collection.md:11).

cards.title: Authentication is symmetric key pinning
items: Both peers present certificates. TLS is 1.3 minimum, and SHA-256 SPKI pins replace CA-chain trust (internal/distributed/identity.go:245-294).
Malformed or duplicate enrollment entries prevent startup. Revoke an agent by removing its entry and restarting the collector (identity.go:175-223; docs/distributed-collection.md:56).

The collector validates incoming frames and records before writing a batch; invalid input is rejected, while a local write failure leaves it eligible for resend (server.go:282-320; docs/distributed-collection.md:77).

cards.title: ACK is a delivery checkpoint
items: Unacknowledged batches are held in memory and resent after reconnects. The default pending budget is 64 MiB; excess backlog can be dropped and counted (client.go:40-66,129-158).
ACK follows gzip flush to the OS, before fsync. Agent process loss can lose queued data; collector host failure can lose acknowledged data (sink.go:120-125; docs/distributed-collection.md:103-105).
Files still being written are unfinished gzip streams. Finalization closes and syncs them; read after shutdown for complete input (sink.go:209-228; docs/distributed-collection.md:106).
